evidence: Modifies src/net_processing.cpp and blockencodings, altering peer message handling and drop-versus-disconnect behavior for malformed blocks and transactions.
rationale: Early rejection of malformed transactions and blocks closes a serious P2P resource exhaustion vector. Without these checks, an attacker could send a 4 MB block containing roughly 400,000 zero-input/zero-output transactions or 16M weight in non-witness transactions, forcing large memory allocations and CPU overhead before validation drops them.
